questions.question: Tippani dance is a traditional folk dance of which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tippani** is a traditional folk dance originating from the **Saurashtra** region of **Gujarat**, specifically from coastal areas like **Chorwad** and **Veraval**.
 
• The dance is exclusively performed by women, particularly those belonging to the **Koli** and **Hali** communities, who traditionally worked as **laborers**.
 
• The name of the dance is derived from the tool used, the **Tippani**, which is a long wooden stick (about **175 cm**) with a wooden or iron block called a **Garbo** at the base.
 
• Historically, the dance evolved from the task of **beating lime** to level the floors and roofs during the construction of houses, where women used the sticks to create a rhythmic beat to alleviate their physical exhaustion.
 
• The performance features dancers striking the **Tippani** against the ground in synchronized movements, creating a powerful percussive rhythm that dictates the pace of the dance.
 
• Musical accompaniment includes folk instruments such as the **Zanj**, **Manjira**, **Tabla**, **Dhol**, and sometimes the **Shehnai**, with dancers singing traditional folk songs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maharashtra**:

 
 
• Famous for **Lavani**, a traditional song and dance genre performed to the beats of the **Dholki**.
 
• Other notable forms include **Koli** (the dance of the fishing community) and **Povada** (ballads describing historical events).
 
 
 
• **Rajasthan**:
 
 
• Renowned for the **Ghoomar** dance, traditionally performed by the **Bhil** tribe for the goddess **Saraswati**.
 
• Other dances include **Kalbelia** (recognized by **UNESCO**) and the balancing-act dance **Bhavai**.
 
 
 
• **Odisha**:
 
 
• Home to the classical dance **Odissi**, which is one of the oldest surviving dance forms in India.
 
• Prominent folk dances include **Chhau** (a martial arts dance), **Ghumura**, and **Sambalpuri**.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat**:
 
 
• Apart from **Tippani**, the state is famous for **Garba** and **Dandiya Raas**, which are globally popular during the **Navratri** festival.
 
• Other folk forms include the **Padhar** dance and the **Bhavai** folk drama.

questions.question: The small percentage of argon in air is approximately:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.93%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Argon (Ar)** is a chemical element with atomic number **18** and is categorized as a **noble gas** within **Group 18** of the periodic table.
 
• In the Earth's atmosphere, **Argon** is the **third-most abundant gas**, comprising approximately **0.934%** (commonly rounded to **0.93%**) of dry air by volume.
 
• This gas is **monatomic** and chemically **inert**, which means it does not form stable chemical compounds at standard temperatures and pressures due to its complete **octet** of valence electrons.
 
• The majority of atmospheric Argon is **Argon-40**, which originates from the **radioactive decay** of **Potassium-40** found in the Earth's crust.
 
• It is significantly more abundant than other noble gases like **Neon** (0.0018%), **Helium** (0.0005%), and **Krypton** (0.0001%), making it the primary inert component after Nitrogen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Major Atmospheric Constituents**:

 
 
• **Nitrogen (78%)**: This is the most prevalent gas in the atmosphere, playing a crucial role in **biological molecules** like proteins and DNA via the **Nitrogen Cycle**.
 
• **Oxygen (21%)**: The second most abundant gas (approximately **20.95%**), essential for **aerobic respiration** and the process of **combustion**.
 
• **Carbon Dioxide (0.03%)**: Historically cited at **0.03%**, though modern levels exceed **0.04%**, it is a critical **greenhouse gas** and is indispensable for **photosynthesis** in plants.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Uses of Argon**:
 
 
• Used extensively in **incandescent lighting** and **fluorescent tubes** to prevent the oxidation of filaments.
 
• Commonly utilized as a **shielding gas** in **Gas Tungsten Arc Welding (GTAW)** to protect the weld area from atmospheric contaminants.
 
• Applied in **cryosurgery** and as a thermal insulator in **energy-efficient windows**.

questions.question: Who was conferred the P.C. Chandra Puraskaar in 2025 for lifetime sporting excellence?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Leander Paes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **P.C. Chandra Puraskaar** is a prestigious annual award established by the **P.C. Chandra Group** in **1993** to honor eminent personalities who have achieved excellence in their respective fields, including sports, culture, and science.
 
• In **2025**, the award was conferred upon the legendary Indian tennis player **Leander Paes** for his unparalleled **lifetime sporting excellence** and his role in placing India on the global tennis map.
 
• **Leander Paes** is celebrated for winning a **Bronze Medal** in the men’s singles category at the **1996 Atlanta Olympics**, which was India’s first individual Olympic medal in 44 years.
 
• Throughout his illustrious career, he has secured **18 Grand Slam titles**, comprising **8 men’s doubles** and **10 mixed doubles** championships, making him one of the most successful doubles players in history.
 
• He is a recipient of India’s highest honors, including the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna** (1996-97), the **Padma Shri** (2001), and the **Padma Bhushan** (2014).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Colonel RS Jamwal**:

 
 
• A highly distinguished **Indian Army officer** and a veteran **mountaineer**.
 
• He is the first Indian to summit **Mount Everest** three times and has successfully scaled the **Seven Summits** (the highest peaks of the seven continents).
 
 
 
• **Ravi Kishan**:
 
 
• A prominent **Indian actor** and **politician** serving as a Member of Parliament.
 
• He is well-known for his extensive work in **Bhojpuri** and **Hindi cinema**, contributing significantly to the regional film industry.
 
 
 
• **Major Kalita**:
 
 
• Refers to a notable officer in the **Indian Armed Forces**, often recognized for gallantry or leadership, though not primarily associated with international sports awards like the P.C. Chandra Puraskaar.

questions.question: The longest glacier in India is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Siachen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Siachen Glacier** is located in the **Karakoram Range** in the **Himalayas**, near the **Line of Control (LoC)** between India and Pakistan.
 
• It is approximately **76 kilometers** (47 miles) long, making it the **longest glacier in India** and the second-longest in the world non-polar regions.
 
• The glacier is strategically significant and is often referred to as the **highest battlefield** in the world, with military posts situated at altitudes exceeding **6,000 meters**.
 
• It serves as the primary source for the **Nubra River**, which flows into the **Shyok River**, a major tributary of the **Indus River** system.
 
• Geographically, it lies just south of the great drainage divide that separates the **Eurasian Plate** from the **Indian subcontinent** in the extensively glaciated portion of the **Karakoram**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gangotri Glacier**:

 
 
• Located in the **Uttarkashi district** of **Uttarakhand**, it is one of the largest glaciers in the **Himalayas** with a length of about **30 kilometers**.
 
• It is the source of the **Bhagirathi River**, which is one of the main headstreams of the **Ganga**.
 
 
 
• **Zemu Glacier**:
 
 
• This is the largest glacier in the **Eastern Himalayas**, situated at the base of **Mount Kangchenjunga** in **Sikkim**.
 
• It has a length of approximately **26 kilometers** and provides water to the **Teesta River**.
 
 
 
• **Pindari Glacier**:
 
 
• Located in the **Kumaon** region of **Uttarakhand**, it is found in the **Bageshwar district**.
 
• It is much smaller than Siachen, with a length of roughly **3 kilometers**, and acts as the source for the **Pindar River**.

questions.question: Who among the following was Akbar's revenue minister credited with land revenue reforms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raja Todar Mal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raja Todar Mal** was the **Finance Minister** (**Mushrif-i-Diwan**) of the **Mughal Empire** during the reign of **Akbar** and was one of the **Navaratnas** (Nine Gems) in his court.
 
• He is primarily credited with the introduction of the **Zabt** or **Dahshala System** in **1580**, which revolutionized the land revenue administration in medieval India.
 
• This system involved a detailed survey of **crop yields** and **market prices** over a **ten-year period** (1570−1580) to calculate a fixed average revenue for each province.
 
• Under his reforms, agricultural land was scientifically measured using a **bamboo jarib** with iron rings, ensuring higher accuracy than the previously used hemp ropes.
 
• The land was classified into four categories based on productivity: **Polaj** (cultivated every year), **Parauti** (left fallow for 1−2 years), **Chachar** (fallow for 3−4 years), and **Banjar** (uncultivated for 5 or more years).
 
• The state share was fixed at **one-third** of the average produce, and taxes were collected primarily in **cash**, which provided fiscal stability to the **Mughal Treasury**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Abul Fazl**:

 
 
• The **Grand Vizier** and official court historian who authored the **Akbarnama** and its detailed third volume, the **Ain-i-Akbari**.
 
 
 
• **Birbal**:
 
 
• Born as **Mahesh Das**, he was a celebrated advisor and **military commander** known for his sharp wit; he was the first and only Hindu to accept the **Din-i-Ilahi** faith.
 
 
 
• **Tansen**:
 
 
• Originally named **Ramtanu Pandey**, he was a legendary **classical musician** and composer in **Akbar’s court**, credited with innovating the **Gwalior Gharana** style.

questions.question: In _____ 2025, Cabinet approved National Sports Policy 2025 of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**July**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Cabinet** of India, chaired by the **Prime Minister**, officially approved the **National Sports Policy 2025** in the month of **July 2025** to revolutionize the country's sports ecosystem.
 
• This landmark policy was introduced to replace the outdated **National Sports Policy 2001**, providing a modern framework that aligns with the **Viksit Bharat 2047** vision of transforming India into a global sporting powerhouse.
 
• A primary focus of the policy approved in **July** is the **decentralization** of sports administration, empowering **State Governments** and **District Sports Authorities** to identify and nurture talent at the grassroots level.
 
• The policy introduces the **National Sports Education Board (NSEB)**, which aims to integrate sports into the formal curriculum under the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**, ensuring that 'sports' is no longer considered just an extra-curricular activity.
 
• The **July 2025** approval facilitates a structured **High-Performance Leadership** model, targeting specific medal outcomes for the **2028 Los Angeles** and **2032 Brisbane Olympic Games**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Core Pillars of the National Sports Policy 2025**:

 
 
• **Digital Transformation**: The policy mandates the creation of a **National Sports Repository**, utilizing **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** for performance mapping and athlete health tracking.
 
• **Athlete Welfare**: Enhancement of the **Pension for Meritorious Sports Persons** scheme and comprehensive insurance coverage for athletes and coaching staff.
 
• **Indigenous Games**: Dedicated funding and national-level competitions for traditional Indian sports like **Kabaddi**, **Mallakhamb**, and **Kalaripayattu** to promote cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Historical Evolution**:
 
 
• The first **National Sports Policy** was formulated in **1984** following India's hosting of the **1982 Asian Games**.
 
• The **2001 Policy** focused on 'Mass Participation' and 'Excellence in Sports', but the **2025 Policy** shifts toward a **Science-Led** and **Governance-Driven** approach to match international standards.

questions.question: TALASH Initiative was launched in July 2025. TALASH stands for ___.

options.text: Tribal Access, Leadership and Skill Hub
Tribal Aptitude, Life Skills and Self-Esteem Hub
Tribal Advancement and Learning Support Hub
Tribal Awareness, Learning, and Social Empowerment Hub

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tribal Aptitude, Life Skills and Self-Esteem Hub**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **TALASH Initiative** is a specialized program launched in **July 2025**, designed to address the socio-economic and educational gaps faced by the **tribal youth** of India.
 
• The acronym stands for **Tribal Aptitude, Life Skills and Self-Esteem Hub**, reflecting a comprehensive strategy that moves beyond traditional academic instruction to foster **holistic personality development**.
 
• The primary objective of the initiative is to identify the **natural aptitude** of tribal students at an early stage, helping them align their career paths with their inherent talents and interests.
 
• By incorporating **Life Skills**, the program ensures that individuals from **Scheduled Tribes (ST)** are equipped with the necessary tools to navigate urban professional environments and modern societal challenges.
 
• The inclusion of the **Self-Esteem Hub** is a critical component aimed at psychological empowerment, helping students overcome **inferiority complexes** and take pride in their **cultural heritage**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Core Components of the TALASH Framework:
 
 
• **Aptitude Assessment**: Utilizing psychometric tools tailored for **diverse linguistic backgrounds** to evaluate logical reasoning and vocational interests.
 
• **Life Skills Curriculum**: Training modules covering **digital literacy**, **financial management**, **critical thinking**, and **effective communication**.
 
• **Self-Esteem Workshops**: Mentorship programs led by **tribal icons** and achievers to build confidence and **leadership qualities**.
 
 
 
• Implementation Strategy:
 
 
• The initiative is predominantly integrated into **Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS)** and **Ashram Schools** across various states.
 
• It leverages partnerships with the **National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC)** to bridge the gap between rural education and **industrial employability**.

questions.question: The Ratha Yatra (cart festival) at Mahesh is the second oldest chariot festival in India, is celebrated in which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mahesh Ratha Yatra** is held in **Mahesh**, a historic neighborhood in **Serampore**, located in the **Hooghly district** of **West Bengal**.
 
• It holds the distinction of being the **second oldest chariot festival** in the world and the oldest in the **Bengal** region, having been celebrated without interruption since **1396 CE**.
 
• The festival was established by **Drubananda Brahmachari**, a **Bengali sadhu**, who, according to legend, received a divine vision of **Lord Jagannath** after being unable to offer bhog at the **Puri Jagannath Temple**.
 
• The **Mahesh Jagannath Temple** houses wooden idols of **Jagannath**, **Balarama**, and **Subhadra**, which are crafted from **neem** wood, following the **Nabakalebara** tradition.
 
• The current grand **iron chariot** was constructed in **1885**, donated by **Krishnachandra Basu**; it stands **50 feet** tall, weighs approximately **125 tonnes**, and moves on **12 wheels**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odisha**:

 
 
• Famous for the **Puri Ratha Yatra**, the oldest and largest chariot festival globally, held at the 12th-century **Jagannath Temple**.
 
• The festival marks the annual journey of the deities to the **Gundicha Temple**.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat**:
 
 
• Hosts the **Ahmedabad Ratha Yatra** at the **Jagannath Temple** in **Jamalpur**, which is the third largest in India.
 
• This tradition was initiated by **Mahant Hanumandasji** in **1878**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance of Mahesh**:
 
 
• Notable 19th-century figures like **Sri Ramakrishna Paramahansa** and **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar** participated in this festival.
 
• The festival is a major cultural event in **Bengal**, accompanied by the **Rathayatra Mela**, which is one of the largest village fairs in the state.

questions.question: As part of the pledge made at COP-26 (Conference of Parties), India's efforts are being directed towards reaching the target of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel electricity capacity by ______.
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

The question refers to India’s enhanced climate action commitments presented at the **COP-26** (Conference of Parties) summit held in **Glasgow** in 2021. Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** announced a five-point plan called **Panchamrit** (Five Nectar Elements) to intensify India’s fight against climate change, focusing on **renewable energy** and **carbon emission** reduction.

Given

 
• Event: **COP-26** Climate Summit.
 
• Target: **500 GW** of **non-fossil fuel** electricity capacity.

Calculation

According to the **Panchamrit** strategy, India set several ambitious milestones to be reached by the end of the current decade. The five pillars of this commitment are:

 
• Reach **500 GW** of **non-fossil fuel** energy capacity by **2030**.
 
• Meet 50% of its energy requirements from **renewable energy** sources by **2030**.
 
• Reduce total projected carbon emissions by one billion tonnes between now and **2030**.
 
• Reduce the carbon intensity of the economy by 45% by **2030**.
 
• Achieve the target of **Net Zero** emissions by the year **2070**.

As per these declarations, the target year for reaching the **500 GW** non-fossil fuel capacity mark is specifically set for **2030**. This initiative is part of India’s updated **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)** to help limit global temperature rise.

Final Answer: ✅ 2030

questions.question: A light year is a measure of ___.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**distance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **light year** is a unit of **distance** rather than time, representing the total path covered by **light** in a **vacuum** over the duration of one **Julian year** (365.25 days).
 
• Light travels at an incredible velocity of approximately **299,792,458 meters per second** (roughly **3 × 10⁸ m/s**); when calculated over a full year, this distance equals approximately **9.46 trillion kilometers** (**9.46 × 10¹² km**).
 
• In the field of **astronomy**, standard terrestrial units like kilometers or miles are insufficient for measuring the immense voids of **interstellar space**, making the light year a fundamental metric for describing gaps between **stars** and **galaxies**.
 
• For instance, the nearest star to Earth (besides the Sun), **Proxima Centauri**, is about **4.24 light years** away, meaning its light takes over four years to reach our planet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Time:** Measured in **seconds**, **minutes**, and **hours**, it defines the duration of events. While 'year' is a unit of time, 'light year' is strictly a spatial measurement.
 
• **Speed:** Refers to the rate of change of position, such as the **speed of light (c)**, which is a universal physical constant.
 
• **Mass:** A fundamental property of matter indicating its resistance to acceleration, typically measured in **kilograms (kg)** or **solar masses** in cosmic contexts.
 
• **Other Astronomical Units:**
 
 
• **Astronomical Unit (AU):** The average distance from the **Earth** to the **Sun**, approximately **150 million kilometers**.
 
• **Parsec (pc):** A unit used for even larger distances, equivalent to approximately **3.26 light years** or **3.08 × 10¹³ km**.

questions.question: Who launched World's First Rocket with Fully 3D Printed Engine in 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Agnikul**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Agnikul Cosmos**, a space-tech startup based in **Chennai**, successfully launched the **Agnibaan SOrTeD** (SubOrbital Technological Demonstrator) mission on **May 30, 2024**.
 
• The mission featured the world’s first **single-piece 3D-printed engine**, named **Agnilet**, which was designed and manufactured entirely in India.
 
• The **Agnilet** engine is a **semi-cryogenic** engine that uses a combination of liquid and gaseous propellants, specifically **Liquid Oxygen (LOX)** and **Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF)**.
 
• This launch was conducted from India's first **private launchpad**, named **Dhanush**, established by Agnikul at the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC) SHAR** in **Sriharikota**.
 
• The 3D-printing technology used, known as **Additive Manufacturing**, allows the entire engine to be printed as a single component, eliminating the need for thousands of parts and joints found in traditional rocket engines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agnikul Cosmos**:

 
 
• Founded in **2017** by Srinath Ravichandran and Moin SPM, the startup is incubated at **IIT Madras**.
 
• The **Agnibaan** rocket is a highly customizable, two-stage launch vehicle capable of carrying payloads of up to **300 kg** to **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)**.
 
 
 
• **Skyroot Aerospace**:
 
 
• Another prominent Indian private space company that launched **Vikram-S**, India's first privately developed rocket, in **November 2022**.
 
 
 
• **Technological Significance**:
 
 
• The successful flight of a **semi-cryogenic engine** is a major milestone for the Indian space sector, as it is more efficient and environment-friendly than solid-fuel engines.
 
• The integration of **3D printing** in aerospace significantly reduces the lead time for engine production from several months to just a few days.

questions.question: What is the name of the initiative launched by the Indian Council of Medical Research in August 2025 to engage school students in science?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ICMR-SHINE**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **ICMR-SHINE** initiative, which stands for **School Health and Health Research Infrastructure for National Education**, was launched to bridge the gap between classroom science and real-world **medical research**.
 
• It specifically targets students in **Classes 9 to 12**, aiming to ignite interest in **biomedical sciences** and **public health** early in their academic journey.
 
• The program provides a structured platform for students to visit **ICMR laboratories**, interact with leading **scientists**, and observe sophisticated **biotechnology** equipment in action.
 
• By fostering a **scientific temper**, the initiative encourages students to understand the methodology behind **evidence-based medicine** and the importance of **clinical research** in solving national health crises.
 
• **ICMR-SHINE** also emphasizes the role of **preventive healthcare**, teaching students about **epidemiology**, **nutrition**, and the mechanics of **disease transmission**.
 
• The initiative is part of a broader strategy to develop a robust pipeline of future **researchers**, **doctors**, and **healthcare professionals** for the **Indian health sector**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR)**:

 
 
• It is the **apex body** in India for the formulation, coordination, and promotion of **biomedical research**.
 
• Established in **1911** as the IRFA and renamed in **1949**, it is funded by the Government of India through the **Department of Health Research**.
 
• ICMR manages a network of **27 national institutes** focusing on diseases like **Tuberculosis**, **Malaria**, and **Cholera**, as well as **nutrition** and **toxicology**.
 
 
 
• **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**:
 
 
• The **ICMR-SHINE** initiative aligns with **NEP 2020**, which advocates for **experiential learning** and **vocational exposure** in schools.
 
• It encourages **interdisciplinary education**, allowing students to see the practical application of **Biology**, **Chemistry**, and **Data Science** in medicine.
 
• Programs like these help in achieving the **STEM** (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) education goals of the **Ministry of Education**.

questions.question: As of July 2025, Dutee Chand holds the ___ metres national record in the women's category.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**100**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dutee Chand** is a celebrated Indian professional sprinter who specializes in the **women's 100 metres** and **200 metres** events.
 
• As of **July 2025**, she remains the holder of the **national record** in the **women's 100 metres** category with a timing of **11.17 seconds**.
 
• She achieved this landmark timing at the **Indian Grand Prix IV** held in **Patiala**, Punjab, on **June 21, 2021**.
 
• By clocking **11.17 seconds**, she broke her own previous national record of **11.22 seconds**, which she had established at the **National Open Athletics Championships** in **Ranchi** in **2019**.
 
• She is the first Indian to win a **gold medal** in a **100m race** at a global stage, achieving this at the **2019 Summer Universiade** in **Naples**, Italy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Career Milestones and Awards**:

 
 
• She secured two **silver medals** at the **2018 Jakarta Asian Games**, one in the **100 metres** and another in the **200 metres** sprint.
 
• In recognition of her outstanding contribution to sports, she was conferred with the **Arjuna Award** in **2020**.
 
• She represented India in the **Summer Olympics** twice, participating in the **2016 Rio Olympics** and the **2020 Tokyo Olympics**.
 
 
 
• **Context of Athletics in India**:
 
 
• The **Athletics Federation of India (AFI)** is the official body responsible for certifying and maintaining **National Records** for various track and field events.
 
• The **100 metres** sprint is the shortest outdoor track event and is considered a flagship event in international athletics competitions like the **World Athletics Championships**.

questions.question: During international competition of Judo, each match lasts for ___ minutes
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In accordance with the official regulations established by the **International Judo Federation (IJF)**, the standard duration for a competitive Judo match in the **Senior** category (for both men and women) is **4 minutes**.
 
• The **4-minute** rule represents **net combat time**, which means the clock is strictly paused whenever the referee calls **Mate** (to temporarily stop the contest) or **Sono-mama** (to freeze positions), and resumes only when the command **Hajime** is given.
 
• This unified timing of **4 minutes** was implemented to ensure **gender equality** across the sport, moving away from previous years where men’s matches lasted 5 minutes while women’s matches were 4 minutes.
 
• In **International Competition**, the same **4-minute** duration applies to the **Junior** age group (under 21), ensuring that athletes transitioning to the senior level are accustomed to the standard match length.
 
• If the **4-minute** regulation time expires and the athletes have equal scores or no scores at all, the match proceeds into an unlimited **Golden Score** period to determine a winner.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Golden Score Overtime**:

 
 
• There is no fixed time limit for the **Golden Score** phase; the first athlete to achieve any score (**Waza-ari** or **Ippon**) or the first to be disqualified by **Hansoku-make** (penalties) wins.
 
• All scores and **Shido** (minor penalties) recorded during the initial **4 minutes** are carried over into this sudden-death period.
 
 
 
• **Primary Scoring Actions**:
 
 
• **Ippon**: The highest score in Judo, awarded for a throw that lands the opponent largely on their back with **strength, speed, and control**, or for a submission (choke or armbar) and pinning for 20 seconds.
 
• **Waza-ari**: Awarded for a throw that lacks one of the elements of an Ippon or for a pin lasting between 10 and 19 seconds. Two **Waza-ari** scores equal an **Ippon**.
 
 
 
• **Age Category Variations**:
 
 
• While senior and junior international matches are **4 minutes**, certain **Cadet** (Under 18) and youth level competitions may occasionally utilize a **3-minute** or **2-minute** format depending on the specific tournament guidelines.

questions.question: What does the electromagnet do once it is activated in an electric bell?

options.text: Pulls the iron strip towards itself

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pulls the iron strip towards itself**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The functioning of an **electric bell** is based on the **magnetic effect of electric current**, where a coil of wire acts as a magnet when electricity passes through it.
 
• The main component is an **electromagnet**, which consists of **insulated copper wire** wound around a **soft iron core**.
 
• When the circuit is completed by pressing the switch, the current flows through the coil, creating a **magnetic field** that transforms the iron core into a temporary magnet.
 
• This **electromagnet** immediately exerts a force of attraction on the **iron strip** (also known as the **armature**) located nearby.
 
• As the **iron strip** is pulled toward the electromagnet, the **hammer** attached to it moves and strikes the **gong**, producing the ringing sound.
 
• This movement also causes the strip to move away from the **contact screw**, which results in the **breaking of the electrical circuit**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Core Components of an Electric Bell:**

 
 
• **Electromagnet**: A temporary magnet that only functions when current is present; the principle was first observed by **Hans Christian Oersted** in **1820**.
 
• **Soft Iron Armature**: Chosen because soft iron has high **magnetic permeability** and low **retentivity**, allowing it to be magnetized and demagnetized rapidly.
 
• **Contact Screw**: Serves as an adjustable component that maintains the **make-and-break** cycle of the circuit.
 
• **Hammer and Gong**: The mechanical parts responsible for converting the kinetic energy of the moving armature into **acoustic energy**.
 
• **Spring Strip**: Provides the restoring force to bring the **iron strip** back to the contact screw once the magnetism is lost, enabling a continuous ringing cycle.

questions.question: Which of the following stringed traditional instrument is found in various parts of North India that provides the basic 'sruti' or 'svara' to the performer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tanpura**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tanpura** (also known as **Tambura**) is a **long-necked plucked string instrument** that serves as a fundamental accompaniment in **Indian Classical Music**.
 
• Its primary role is to provide a continuous **harmonic drone** or **sruti** (pitch reference), allowing the lead vocalist or instrumentalist to maintain **svara** (tonal accuracy) throughout the performance.
 
• In the **Hindustani (North Indian)** tradition, the instrument is typically crafted from **Tun wood** or **teak** and features a large dried **gourd** (tumba) as a resonator.
 
• The instrument usually consists of **four, five, or six strings** made of steel and bronze, which are plucked in a rhythmic sequence to produce a rich spectrum of **overtones**.
 
• The unique sound of the Tanpura is generated by the **Jivari** (the bridge), which is curved in a way that allows the strings to vibrate against the surface, creating a distinctive **buzzing timbre**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khartal**:

 
 
• An **ancient percussion instrument** (idiophone) made of wood or metal clappers.
 
• It is primarily used in **folk music** of **Rajasthan** and **Gujarat** and is widely played during **Bhajans** and **Sufi** devotional singing.
 
 
 
• **Pavo**:
 
 
• A traditional **double-barrel flute** or wind instrument found in **Gujarat**.
 
• It is commonly used by **pastoral communities** like the **Ahirs** and requires the technique of **circular breathing** to produce a continuous melody.
 
 
 
• **Pakhawaj**:
 
 
• A **barrel-shaped, two-headed drum** that is the standard percussion accompaniment for the **Dhrupad** style of North Indian music.
 
• It is regarded as the North Indian version of the **Mridangam** and is known for its deep, low-frequency resonance.

questions.question: Which of the following nuclei are commonly used in nuclear fusion reactions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydrogen and its isotopes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nuclear fusion** is the process where two light atomic nuclei combine to form a single heavier nucleus, a transformation that releases a vast amount of energy due to the conversion of mass into energy according to **Einstein mass-energy equivalence**.
 
• The primary nuclei used in this process are **Hydrogen and its isotopes**, specifically **Deuterium (²H)** and **Tritium (³H)**, because their low atomic number (Z=1) results in the lowest possible **Coulombic repulsion** between nuclei.
 
• The **Deuterium-Tritium (D-T) reaction** is the most widely pursued for energy production because it has a high reaction cross-section at relatively lower temperatures, roughly **150 million degrees Celsius**.
 
• A single D-T fusion event produces a **Helium-4** nucleus and a high-energy **neutron**, yielding approximately **17.6 MeV** of energy per reaction.
 
• While **Deuterium** is abundantly found in Earth oceans, **Tritium** is rare and is typically bred from **Lithium** within the fusion reactor blanket during operation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Uranium and Thorium**:

 
 
• These are heavy elements used in **nuclear fission**, where large, unstable nuclei split into smaller fragments, a process currently used in commercial nuclear power plants.
 
• **Uranium-235** and **Plutonium-239** are common fissile fuels, while **Thorium-232** is a fertile material central to India **three-stage nuclear power program**.
 
 
 
• **Carbon and Nitrogen**:
 
 
• These elements are key components of the **CNO (Carbon-Nitrogen-Oxygen) cycle**, a catalytic fusion process occurring in stars that are more massive than our Sun.
 
 
 
• **Helium and Oxygen**:
 
 
• **Helium-3** is considered a potential future fuel for **aneutronic fusion**, which would produce fewer neutrons, making energy capture safer and more efficient.
 
• **Oxygen** fusion occurs naturally during the advanced stages of stellar evolution in very high-mass stars after **Helium** and **Neon** burning phases.
